bootstrap.type: circular moving-block (Politis-Romano), percentile CI; block length capped at n/4 for windows < 20 points

conventions.tokens: tokens = step x 262,144 (cumulative tokens through the logged optimizer step); the logged loss at step N is the mean token CE (nats) of that single optimizer step's 262,144-token batch, computed before the update (not a window average)
conventions.gap: first minus second run, nats per token, same logged step; positive = first run has the higher loss
conventions.last_half: logged steps 960..1900 (tokens 0.2517..0.4981 B), i.e. strictly after step 953.5 = half of 1907; steps 1901-1907 are not logged
conventions.slope_units: nats per 1B tokens; 'change over the last half' = slope x 0.25B tokens

data_quality.interpretation: all six residual correlations lie within +-0.18 and the same-seed pairs (dense/MoE-42/NESTOR) are not more correlated than the cross-seed pairs; shared batches at a given step would give strongly positive correlations, so there is no evidence that seed 42 pairs the data across architectures (the sampler seed is drawn from the global RNG after model initialisation, which differs by architecture). Per-step noise is therefore treated as independent between runs.

gap.method: local-linear LOESS, tricube, window = k nearest logged points
gap.rule: largest k whose pooled leave-one-out CV MSE (4 main gap series) is within 1% of the minimum

curve.method: local-quadratic LOESS, tricube, window = k nearest logged points
curve.rule: largest k whose pooled leave-one-out CV MSE (4 loss curves) is within 1% of the minimum

smoothing.use: smooth curves and bands are for display only; all slopes, means and CIs are computed on the raw logged points

schedule.type: cosine annealing with linear warmup: torch SequentialLR([LambdaLR(step/warmup), CosineAnnealingLR(T_max, eta_min)], milestones=[warmup]); all param groups share the multiplier
schedule.source: repo nestor/experiments/pretrain.py (CosineAnnealingConfig(T_max=max_steps, warmup_steps=0.08*max_steps, eta_min=1e-5)); nestor/train/optim.py build_scheduler/_create_warmup_scheduler; paper Table 12 (warmup linear 8 % of steps, cosine, minimum 1e-5)

this_reproduction.h100_runs: config.json not stored locally; launcher scripts modal/prod.sh and modal/moe2.sh pass --steps 1907 --warmup 153 (copies in inputs/launchers); logged lr identical in shape (see verification)

schedule.formula: m(N) = N/W for N < W; m(N) = [eta_min + (peak - eta_min) * (1 + cos(pi (N - W) / T_max)) / 2] / peak for N >= W, where N = number of optimizer steps already taken (the lr used by update N+1)

heldout_stageA.source: reproduction_stageA.json (fp32 CE, val09 first 10,004,085 tokens of shard 09; val10 first 5,004,090 tokens of shard 10)

paper_comparison.note: held-out sets differ (paper: its own DCLM split; here: global shard 09 file 0 first 10.0M tokens = val09, shard 10 first 5.0M tokens = val10); only differences between architectures on one evaluation set are compared.

caveats: Each logged loss is the mean CE of ONE optimizer step (262,144 tokens, before the update), logged every 10th step (190 of 1,907 steps per run; steps 1901-1907 are not logged); per-point noise about the smooth curve is SD 0.039 nats per run (a gap: 0.059).

The four runs do not share batches (residual correlations between runs -0.12..+0.18; same-seed pairs -0.02 vs cross-seed pairs +0.14 on average), so seed 42 does not pair the data across architectures and paired differences do not cancel batch noise.

The seed noise reference is ONE MoE seed pair (1 d.o.f.) and also contains the platform difference (seed 43 on H100, seed 42 on the local GPU); read it as an order of magnitude. NESTOR-MoE(seed 43) is H100 vs H100 and NESTOR-MoE(seed 42) is H100 vs local; the two differ by +0.013 nats (last-half means), which equals the seed-reference mean by construction.

NESTOR is a single run (seed 42): the NESTOR-MoE(seed 42) and NESTOR-MoE(seed 43) curves share it and are not independent evidence of the gap; NESTOR's own seed variability is unknown (the MoE seed pair is the only seed reference available).

Peak learning rates differ by architecture (largest Muon group: dense 0.0200, MoE 0.01155, NESTOR 0.02828; Muon base 0.01 times a matrix-shape scale), so 'same recipe' is not the same effective LR; whether each architecture is near its LR optimum at a 10x shorter horizon is untested.

Tokens and the LR multiplier are perfectly collinear within one run (cosine: 0.62 of peak at the start of the last half, 0.018 at step 1900), so a slope in the last half cannot separate a token effect from an annealing effect.

The first 0.4B tokens of the paper's 5B run are warmup (1,526 steps) whereas this run warms up in 0.04B tokens: the early phase in which the NESTOR deficit appears (steps 250-350, 0.07-0.09B tokens, LR near peak) has no counterpart at the same token count in the 5B run (LR 0.17-0.22 of peak there).

Held-out comparison with the paper mixes different evaluation sets (paper: its own DCLM split; here: shard-09/shard-10 slices), different data order (authors: DistributedSampler seed 0; here: single-GPU RandomSampler) and a single seed per cell; only between-architecture differences on one evaluation set are compared.
deviations: No reduction in data scope: all four logs were parsed in full (190 of 190 logged points per run, 760 rows); the logs themselves contain only every 10th step and not steps 1901-1907.

Method not performed, by instruction: power-law (or any other) extrapolation of the gap to the 5B-token budget. The design asked for power-law extrapolations; task item 4 forbids naive extrapolation across the LR schedule. The within-run trend is reported descriptively only.

outputs/*_b05/*/ contain only config.json (local runs) and checkpoints, no logs; the local logs are logs/pretrain_{dense,moe}_100m_b05.log, the local NESTOR log is a stub (NESTOR was trained on the H100) and the H100 artifact logs were used for NESTOR and MoE seed 43. Input copies and sha256 are in inputs/.

The two H100 runs have no config.json on disk: their schedule is established from the launcher scripts (--steps 1907 --warmup 153) and verified against the logged lr (max residual 5.2e-5, within 4-decimal rounding), not from a stored config.

Smoothing span (leave-one-out CV with a 1 % smoothing-favoured rule; display only), block length (5 logged points), bootstrap sizes and the definition of the last half (logged steps 960-1900) are analysis choices of this report; sensitivity results are stored under gaps.*.robustness.
